To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
underfeeding decreased the LPL activity only in cardiac muscle, while refeeding enhanced LPL activity in all tissues, but not the GLUT4 protein content in perirenal adipose tissue.
the variations in food supply induce divergent variations of LPL activity and GLUT4 protein content in adipose tissues and muscle in adult cattle.
underfeeding decreases lipolysis in adipose tissue and oxidative muscle, and refeeding increases lipolysis in both adipose tissue and muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nutritional regulation of lipogenesis and lipolysis in bovine AT and muscle.
the regulation of LPL and GLUT4 in AT and skeletal muscles of adult cattle in relation to nutritional status.
the regulation of lipid metabolism in AT and muscle in ruminant animals and the regulation of LPL and GLUT4 in AT, and of LPL in muscles in response to underfeeding and refeeding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of LPL and GLUT4 protein content in bovine AT and muscles is more complex than in rats, but is also more flexible to variations in nutritional supply.
, under the nutritional conditions tested, the regulation of LPL activity in AT and skeletal muscle in cattle differs from the regulation of LIP in AT and muscle in non- ruminants.

the variations in the nutritional supply of cattle are associated with divergent changes in GLUT4 protein contents between AT and muscles, whereas variations in LPL activity are similar in AT and muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nutritional regulation of LPL is tissue specific in ruminant animals, while the regulation of GLUT4 is specific to AT in cattle.

, in ruminant animals, the variations in LPL activity and GLUT4 content in AT and muscle are not coordinated, and that the nutritional regulation of GLUT4 content in bovine AT is different from that of muscle.
, in bovine, the nutritional regulation of LPL and GLUT4 is different in AT and muscles and is tissue-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nutritional regulation of lipoprotein uptake and glucose transport is tissue-specific in ruminants.

the regulation of lipid and glucose metabolism in AT and muscles in ruminants is not similar to that observed in monogastric species, and that the response to variations in food intake is tissue-specific.
the nutritional status induces divergent changes of GLUT4 and LPL in AT and skeletal muscles in adult cattle.
